title: relayConfig
responsibility: Declares operator controls for relay request limits, pairing capacity and device traffic.

configControls.name: relayConfig.bodyBytes
configControls.purpose: Bound accepted request bodies to protect relay memory.

configControls.name: relayConfig.rateWindowMs
configControls.purpose: Choose the time window used to budget public pairing calls.

configControls.name: relayConfig.pairingCalls
configControls.purpose: Set pairing request capacity for expected device traffic.

configControls.name: relayConfig.failedConnects
configControls.purpose: Bound failed connection attempts before rate limiting a host.

configControls.name: relayConfig.openPairings
configControls.purpose: Limit simultaneous pairing offers retained for each host.

configControls.name: relayConfig.frameWindowMs
configControls.purpose: Choose the interval used to budget device frames.

configControls.name: relayConfig.deviceFrames
configControls.purpose: Set device frame capacity for expected interactive traffic.

configControls.name: relayConfig.sweepDelayMs
configControls.purpose: Set how long expired offers remain available to polling devices.

outputs.name: relayConfig
outputs.type: { readonly internalOrigin: "https://relay.internal"; readonly bodyBytes: number; readonly tlsEnvironments: readonly ["production", "staging"]; readonly rateWindowMs: 60000; readonly pairingCalls: 600; readonly failedConnects: 20; readonly openPairings: 64; readonly frameWindowMs: 10000; readonly deviceFrames: 1200; readonly sweepDelayMs: 2500; }
outputs.description: The `relayConfig` object exported from `packages/relay/src/configs/networking-security/relayConfig.ts` and re-exported by `packages/relay/src/configs/relayConfig.ts`, holding the bounds the contract leaves to the relay: the JSON body read limit, the rate and frame windows, the pairing, failed-connect, offer and device-frame limits, the expired-offer retention, the internal host origin (never resolved: a namespace binding carries the request) and the environments where nothing is served over plain HTTP. Each value matters where the relay applies it, as the source comments describe, and the values are written in the source: protocol limits are not part of this object, and the doc comment above the export names them `remoteLimits`.
